title: Who bears the cost of forecast error? code and data release
description:
Code and derived data release for the manuscript Who bears the cost of forecast error? Performance metrics as regulation in China's wind and solar settlement.

The study uses three years of settled day-ahead schedules from a southern Chinese provincial grid (2023, 2024, and a partial 2025) to compare two official accuracy formulas that differ only in their denominator: the national capacity-normalised index and the regional index with realised output floored at 20% of capacity. On the 2024 analysis sample of 15,191 farm-days, the regional score-minimising report lies 27-30% below the mean, identical forecasts score 62 regionally and 88 nationally, and the 20.5-point provincial-plant gap decomposes into 3.0 points of capacity weighting, 31.0 of error cancellation and -13.6 from the denominator. Under the existing thresholds, a reference-curve denominator shifts compliance from 60.5% to 49.8%; a common recalibrated threshold of 53.4 restores the aggregate pass rate.

The archive contains the analysis code, derived farm-day panels, result tables and figures. The raw 15-minute metered output and settled schedules are confidential and are not included; no de-identified sample is available. Code is released under MIT; derived tables and figures under CC BY 4.0.
